content: A chemical burn is an injury that occurs when living tissue comes into contact with a reactive chemical substance, such as a strong acid or base. The primary types of substances that can cause chemical burns include acids, bases, oxidizing agents, solvents, and reducing agents. When these chemicals come into contact with the skin, they can cause localized damage to the skin itself, systemic effects throughout the body, or both. There are various causes of chemical burns. For example, sparklers and other fireworks that emit sparks or flames can cause chemical burns in addition to burns caused by heat. Other common sources of chemical burns include substances such as silver nitrate (AgNO3), hydrochloric acid (HCl), lye (sodium hydroxide, NaOH), and lime (calcium oxide, CaO). Chemical burns can occur through direct contact with the skin or eyes, inhalation of chemical fumes, or ingestion of the chemical substance. These include professions in chemical manufacturing, mining, medicine, and other related fields.
